support.quote: She is best known for her 1955 refusal to move from her seat on a bus in Montgomery, Alabama, in defiance of Jim Crow racial segregation laws
Rosa Parks, an African American, was arrested that day for violating a city law requiring racial segregation of public buses.

assessments.note: The driver had told her to move back to give up her seat; she refused.

support.quote: On April 10, Circuit Judge W. A. Jenkins Jr. issued a blanket injunction against "parading, demonstrating, boycotting, trespassing and picketing". Leaders of the campaign announced they would disobey the ruling.
King’s 12 April 1963 arrest for violating Alabama’s law against mass public demonstrations took place just over a week after the campaign’s commencement.

assessments.note: Describes the charge as a demonstration law rather than the injunction; both refer to marching despite the ban (noted in the article notes).

support.quote: Cassius Clay refused today, as expected, to take the one step forward that would have constituted induction into the armed forces.

assessments.note: Contemporary report, 29 April 1967.

support.quote: There was no immediate Government action.

assessments.note: Refutes the old premise that Ali was arrested in Houston on 28 April 1967; the wording now asks why he was stripped of his title and convicted.

support.quote: At the trial on June 20, 1967, the jury found Ali guilty after only 21 minutes of deliberation of the criminal offense of violating the Selective Service laws by refusing to be drafted.
Anthony was arrested on November 18, 1872, by a U.S. Deputy Marshal and charged with illegally voting.
1872 – Anthony is arrested for voting in the front parlor of 7 Madison Street (now 17 Madison) on November 18 and is indicted in Albany.
At 12.45 a.m. arrested at Karadi near Dandi for violating Salt Law, without trial was imprisoned and released on 26 January, 1931 unconditionally.
However, Gandhi was arrested on the midnight of 4–5 May 1930, just days before the planned action at Dharasana.

assessments.note: Wikipedia's Gandhi article adds he was interned under a regulation dating from 1827 (noted in the article notes).
